name: homologia
description: Establish whether an on-chain computation and its off-chain reimplementation agree, integer for integer, over declared vectors.

interface.shortDescription: Establish whether an on-chain computation and its off-chain reimplementation agree, integer for integer, over declared vectors.
interface.longDescription: A protocol's arithmetic gets written twice: once in Solidity, where it runs in unsigned 256-bit integers with an explicit rounding direction and a ray or wad scale, and again off-chain in a TypeScript SDK or a Python analytics job, where it runs in doubles, BigInt or Decimal with the token decimals applied by hand. Nothing in an ordinary test suite compares the two. A fuzzing campaign asks whether the contract agrees with itself; a lint asks whether a signing prompt is readable, not whether its number is right. Homologia takes one pinned pair, a contract computation and one off-chain mirror, and a declared vector set whose expected answers carry a provenance class, then reports whether the pair agrees integer for integer and preserves every divergence as a specimen. Exact equality is the default and a tolerance has to be declared and is echoed in the verdict it weakens. A verdict says the pair agrees; it never says either side is correct, because two implementations of the same misunderstanding agree perfectly.
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $homologia to check whether this contract computation and its off-chain mirror agree over declared vectors.
